learn.prompt: A 20 N load sits 2 m left of the pivot. Move the 10 N effort until the beam balances.
learn.hint: The load makes 20 N x 2 m = 40 N m of torque. Find the effort distance that makes the same torque.
learn.explanation: The load torque is 20 N x 2 m = 40 N m. A 10 N effort needs 40 N m / 10 N = 4 m to match it.

learn.prompt: A fixed effort is moved twice as far from the pivot. What happens to its torque?
learn.hint: Torque grows in direct proportion to the distance from the pivot.
learn.explanation: Torque = force x distance. Doubling the distance doubles the torque when the force is unchanged.

misconceptionMap.b: Moving farther from the pivot makes the effort more effective, not less.
misconceptionMap.c: The force is unchanged, but torque also depends on distance from the pivot.
misconceptionMap.d: Quadrupling would require doubling both force and distance.

check.prompt: A 30 N load sits 1.5 m left of the pivot. Place the 15 N effort so the beam balances.
check.hint: Compute the load torque first, then divide by the effort force.
check.explanation: Load torque = 30 N x 1.5 m = 45 N m. The 15 N effort must sit 45 N m / 15 N = 3 m from the pivot.

check.prompt: A 12 N load sits 2 m left of a pivot. How far right of the pivot must an 8 N effort be placed to balance it?
check.hint: Set load torque equal to effort torque: 12 N x 2 m = 8 N x d.
check.explanation: 12 N x 2 m = 24 N m, and 24 N m / 8 N = 3 m.

misconceptionMap.a: That divides the load force by the effort force but ignores the load distance.
misconceptionMap.b: That copies the load distance. The effort is smaller, so it must sit farther out.
misconceptionMap.d: That gives 32 N m of effort torque, which is more than the load torque.

takeaway.title: A small force far out can match a large force close in
takeaway.body: Torque is force times distance from the pivot. A lever balances when the two torques are equal, so moving an effort farther out multiplies its turning effect.
